result:
Favorites are in. `swift build` succeeds and `swift test` passes all 54 tests, including the 5 new ones. I didn't commit anything and didn't touch the fixtures. I also haven't run the UI, so the heart button and favorites screen are compile-checked only.

- **Storage:** `Services/FavoritesStore.swift` has the `FavoritesStore` protocol and `UserDefaultsFavoritesStore`, which takes an injectable `UserDefaults`. It stores the full `Movie` values as JSON in insertion order and drops duplicate ids on load and save.
- **Model changes:** `Movie` is now `Codable`. It encodes to the same keys and `yyyy-MM-dd` date format it already decodes, so it round-trips through `JSONDecoder.tmdb`. I added `TMDBDate.string(from:)` for the date and `Movie.init(detail:)` so the detail screen can favorite a `Movie`.
- **View model:** `ViewModels/FavoritesViewModel.swift` is `@Observable` and `@MainActor`, with `favorites`, `isFavorite(_:)`, `toggle(_:)` and `remove(at:)`. Every change is saved to the store.
- **Views:** `Views/FavoritesView.swift` is a list with swipe to delete and an empty state. `MovieDetailView` gets a heart toolbar button that shows once the movie has loaded.
- **Tests:** `Tests/TMDBAppTests/FavoritesTests.swift` covers toggle on/off, persistence across store instances, order, removal and no duplicates. Each test uses its own `UserDefaults` suite, wipes it afterward, and takes its movies from the `popular_page1` fixture.

`MovieDetailView` and `FavoritesView` read `FavoritesViewModel` from the SwiftUI environment and will crash if nothing provides it. The package has no root `App` or `TabView`, so nothing injects it yet. The host app needs one `FavoritesViewModel()` passed down with `.environment(...)` and a `FavoritesView(service:)` tab.
